SOURCE_CORE_PROPOSITION: Graph contraction, coarsening and quotient graphs/networks give formal language: Loukas (many-to-one map, contraction sets, induced partition), Sánchez-García (partition characteristic matrix; quotient networks can be directed and weighted), Xiao et al. 2008 (network quotients, structural coarse-graining)

Sánchez-García distinguishes normalized quotient Q(A)=Λ^{-1}S^T A S from unnormalized compression B=S^T A S; the paper treats characteristic-matrix aggregation only as precedent and adopts a structurally analogous unnormalized block-sum Q=M^T R_P M by Reference-evidence multiplicity, not identical to the literature's normalized definition; term roles: contraction (merge block nodes), membership-induced graph coarsening (process), weighted directed quotient network (resulting object)

Division of labour: Reference Coupling explains why cross-references are SE relation evidence; coarsening/quotient literature supplies partition/contraction/aggregation language; combined to define paper-specific RefQ and RefQN; partition from semantic membership, not symmetry/automorphism/equitable/spectral; no spectral-preservation, lossless-compression or Loukas locality guarantees inherited

RefQ must be distinguished from common projections: Kessler's bibliographic coupling is a second-order relation induced by shared cited objects, not the same construction as Blincoe's direct aggregation; the paper does not build QQ^T, Q^T Q or K=XΦX^T; core object is Q=M^T R_P M (first-order membership-induced quotient)

DBMS projects involve query processing, transactions, concurrency, storage, logging/recovery, replication, data models and interface compatibility; DBMS extensibility and adoption-context studies suggest these are worth domain observation; they make cross-project/tool-chain Reference evidence a testable motivation, without asserting DBMS differs from all other software

SOURCE_CORE_PROPOSITION: RefQ's empirical meaning lies not in reading GitHub References as code dependency or task resolution but in placing traceable fine-grained evidence within an explicit project-level construction boundary; RQ1 shows why eligibility and project mapping must precede project-level structure — evidence comes from discussion, external resources and internal contexts and cannot be folded directly into topology; RefQ complements package-dependency/code-call views by retaining explicit collaborative references

RQ2a–c distinguish three observation roles rather than repeating one metric: source activity, target coverage, first-order structural position; source/target asymmetry is the interpretation contract of the seed-centred observed graph, not a reporting detail; central positions and brokerage candidates are observed network positions, not project importance, governance effectiveness or causal knowledge-flow mechanisms

RQ3 shows DBMS subdomain differences are local, metric-dependent and label-mode sensitive; supports retaining label-mode and metric-type boundaries when interpreting RefQ relations, not generalising category variation into an ecosystem-wide regularity

Prior direct project-reference aggregation, extraction/identity handling and quotient/coarsening vocabulary give empirical and mathematical precedents; the paper does not claim novelty for aggregation, direction, count weighting or generic coarsening, nor presents RefQ as replacing Reference Coupling; the bounded methodological contribution is formalising/reframing these operations as checkable eligibility, membership, aggregation, observation and interpretation contracts

Formalisation lets observable and quotient-eligible evidence be tracked separately, roles be interpreted within their own boundaries, and project-level relations remain traceable to evidence; DBMS discussion contexts (specs, drivers, tool chains, test frameworks, implementation experience) give domain background; "discussion-driven" only describes concentration in discussion contexts and implies no collaboration culture, causal knowledge exchange or task-resolution mechanism

RefQ construction entails coarse-graining information loss: specific semantics of fine-grained References are compressed; edge weight is only aggregated evidence multiplicity, not motive or strength of each reference; membership-resolution errors propagate into the quotient relation; RefQ's value is a traceable, interpretable project-level structural view, not a replacement for fine-grained semantic analysis

Bounded uses: screening source-active projects; identifying targets with broader coverage under seed-centred observation; locating bridge-like structural candidates; prioritising qualitative/manual review cases; organising explicit Reference evidence for ecosystem analysis; candidate level only — not project quality ranking, governance judgement or automated maintenance decisions

Stronger downstream use requires Reference semantic classification, manual validation, longitudinal evidence where temporal judgements are involved, and task- and domain-matched validation; only then can project-level relations support questions beyond candidate screening and evidence organisation

Three-layer synthesis (construction boundary → structural characterisation → domain comparison): RQ1 evidence-boundary support; RQ2a–c structural centre; RQ3 subdomain comparison and label-mode sensitivity; observation roles, operators and denominators are not interchangeable

RefQ is a traceable weak-semantic project-level structural relation: RQ1 constrains its evidence base, RQ2 gives role-based characterisation, RQ3 supports only bounded local comparison; algorithmic communities and brokerage candidates remain positions in the current view, not stable semantic communities, organisational mechanisms or causal conclusions

SOURCE_CORE_PROPOSITION: RefQ is a defined construct; project-level quotient is structural aggregation, not dependency ground truth or task-resolution relation; the same link may mean implementation reference, duplicate, dependency note, spec, bug report, automated relation or information; implicit references in natural language, screenshots, version notes may escape rule-based extraction; no per-reference semantic classification, so "discussion-driven" and "external-resource orientation" are empirical descriptions from aggregate statistics, not causal mechanisms of knowledge flow

Internal: threats from extraction, entity validation, membership mapping/repository resolution and quotient construction; GitHub Docs describe autolink and PR–Issue syntax; IREL gives the rule framework; GH_CoRE uses rules, regex and API validation; may miss version numbers, short hashes, URL variants, dead links, implicit references or include ambiguous matches — a limitation of the method, not an empirical error rate from the docs; entity-type and membership errors propagate; automated events may amplify some types; aggregation loses artifact semantics

Mitigation: text normalisation, reachability checks, attribute completion, upstream duplicate control and multiplicity checks, entity-type review, membership and construction checks; metric interpretation distinguishes referencing/referenced entities, self-reference, non-project references and RefQ relations; not framed as classifier validation; controls reduce but do not eliminate extraction and membership error; provenance supports review

External: active OSS DBMS projects on GitHub meeting the criteria; not directly generalisable to closed-source DBMS, enterprise databases, non-GitHub projects or low-activity projects; platform mechanisms, syntax, review culture and automation may change how references are observable

DBMS technical/maintenance context limits extrapolation to web frameworks, ML libraries, mobile apps or cloud-native infrastructure; systematic cross-domain differences need dedicated comparison; current RefQN is seed-centred: 294 seeds complete source observation, expanded targets not symmetric; findings are bounded to the OSS DBMS setting, not a complete GitHub network or universal OSS regularity
